my_lead: 12 - abstract: 'culminating in the discovery of 12, an orally bioavailable and selective FD inhibitor'

reactions.issue: B2pin2 contributes the Bpin group, so listing it is right; origin 'reagent' is not 'commercial' but the paper gives its CAS and says reagents were from suppliers.

Two distinct transformations (Boc removal with HCl/dioxane, then ester hydrolysis with LiOH) are merged into one step. The paper concentrates the amino ester to dryness and adds LiOH to the resulting solid without characterising it. The step is only valid if that telescoped procedure counts as one reaction.

notes: Procedure is the compound 12 entry (Experimental, ~lines 923-975) plus compound 25 (line 1210). Leaves: methyl 2-(2-hydroxyphenyl)acetate (CAS 22446-37-3), 3-bromobenzyl bromide (CAS 823-78-9) and the Boc bromo amino alcohol (CAS 910308-92-8, no preparation; 'chiral starting materials were commercially available with ee >=98%') are all given by CAS number and the general statement says reagents came from commercial suppliers. SMILES: I re-derived the stereocentre by hand; N[C@H](CO)Ar is (S), matching the name in both the Boc bromide and the final product. All names match the SMILES. BORDERLINE STEP COUNT: 4 only if Boc removal + hydrolysis is one step; counted as two chemical reactions it is 5 and fails the limit. Maintainer should decide; I consider the amino ester a real (unisolated) intermediate. Quote: 'HCl in 1,4-dioxane ... was then added to (S)-methyl 2-(...)acetate (9.0 g) and the mixture was stirred 2 h. The mixture was then directly concentrated to dryness, and to the resulting solid was added THF, MeOH, water followed by LiOH.'
